To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the weak decay of a heavy meson into two quarks is dominated by the three quark jet configuration and that the jet distribution of the heavy quark jet in the decay of the heavy meson can be calculated from the jet distributions in e+e− experiments.

the weak decay of a heavy-quark pair into two jets has an effect on the jet distributions that is comparable to that of the QCD process e+e− → qq¯, but that this effect is not large enough to be observed at the current level of statistics.
the weak decay of a heavy pair of quarks can lead to jet-like distributions, and that these jet-like distributions can be used to study the properties of the heavy quark.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weak decay of a heavy meson pair in e+e− experiments is dominated by three quark jets and the jet-like distributions for the heavy quark jets are similar to those for light quark jets.
the three quarks jet configuration dominates over the tw quarks jet configuration and the jet distributions are sensitive to the heavy quark mass.
the three-quark-jets are found to be more spheric than the two-quark jets, and the sphericity and spherocity of the quark jets are found to be independent of the heavy quark masses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the jet distributions for the weak decay of a heavy meson pair can be used as a probe of the underlying dynamics of the heavy quark production and decay.
the jet distributions from heavy quark decays can be used to study the weak interaction of heavy quarks.
the jet distributions are not significantly altered by the presence of heavy quarks and their subsequent weak decay.
